documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside regional hospital emergency department. Visit 04/08/2025, 07:05-12:20.

CC: palpitations and lightheadedness.
HPI: 62-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, poorly controlled hypertension, CAD with LAD stent, essential tremor, CML on imatinib and colon cancer on capecitabine, who felt sudden rapid heartbeat and lightheadedness about 20 minutes into a morning jog. No syncope, no chest pain. Takes flecainide 100 mg twice daily (cardiology, since 11/2024) and metoprolol.
Home medications (per pharmacy list): lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, aspirin 81 mg, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg, imatinib 400 mg, capecitabine 1500 mg twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father HTN, essential tremor, MI at 62; mother type 2 diabetes; older brother colorectal cancer at 61.
Social: former smoker, quit 2013, 20 pack-years; 1-2 drinks a week; office administrator.

Exam on arrival: BP 130/85, HR 160 irregular, RR 18. Anxious, alert. Lungs clear. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.
Labs: sodium 140 mEq/L, potassium 4.2 mEq/L, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, troponin I <0.01 ng/mL.
ECG: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response and a widened QRS. His earlier ECGs show atrial fibrillation with a normal QRS.

MDM: exertional rapid AF with rate-related QRS widening on a class IC agent - consistent with flecainide adverse effect. Flecainide held. On continuous monitoring his rate slowed and he converted spontaneously to sinus rhythm at about 11:40 with a narrow QRS on repeat ECG. Asymptomatic afterward.

Disposition: discharged home 12:20. Stop flecainide until seen by cardiology. Continue metoprolol. No jogging until cleared. Cardiology follow-up within 2 weeks; primary care within a week.
Diagnoses: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; flecainide adverse effect.

medications.reason: Held by oncology for chemotherapy-induced pancytopenia

reports.text: BONE MARROW ASPIRATE AND CORE BIOPSY, posterior iliac crest. Clinical: CML on imatinib, colon adenocarcinoma on capecitabine, new pancytopenia. Core: hematopoietic precursors of all lineages show markedly increased apoptotic bodies. Immunohistochemistry: increased p53 and BAX expression in hematopoietic precursors. Blasts not increased (CD34 under 2%). No metastatic carcinoma. Aspirate: maturing trilineage elements with increased apoptotic forms; no dysplasia.
reports.conclusion: Marrow with markedly increased precursor apoptosis, consistent with cytotoxic therapy effect. No increase in blasts; no evidence of CML progression. No metastatic carcinoma.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology visit and marrow report
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology/hematology clinic. Date of service: 09/29/2025; marrow final 10/03/2025.

HPI: 62-year-old with stage IV colon adenocarcinoma on capecitabine since 09/2022 and chronic-phase CML on imatinib, with two weeks of profound fatigue. Routine cycle labs show pancytopenia.

Medications: lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metoprolol succinate 50 mg, aspirin 81 mg, isosorbide mononitrate ER 30 mg, imatinib 400 mg daily, capecitabine 1500 mg twice daily days 1-14 q21d.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father hypertension, essential tremor, MI at 62; mother type 2 diabetes; older brother colorectal cancer at 61.
Social: office administrator; former smoker (20 pack-years); 1-2 drinks weekly.

Labs 09/29: WBC 1.9, ANC 0.8, hemoglobin 8.7, platelets 64.
Bone marrow biopsy 09/29: markedly increased apoptotic bodies in hematopoietic precursors with increased p53 and BAX by immunohistochemistry; blasts not increased.

Assessment: chemotherapy-induced pancytopenia from capecitabine. No sign of CML progression.
Plan: hold capecitabine. Continue imatinib 400 mg daily. CBC weekly; transfuse for hemoglobin under 7 or bleeding. Neutropenic precautions and fever instructions reviewed. Revisit in 4-6 weeks.

documents.body:
Yearly exam (delayed from last fall). 63 yo.
Interval: chemotherapy-related pancytopenia last fall, recovered; capecitabine resumed at 1000 mg BID d1-14 q21d. Flecainide stopped April 2025 after the ED visit; no AF since. CT Feb stable; next CT this summer with oncology.
Feels well. Working, walking and jogging easy miles. Tremor unchanged.
Meds: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succinate 50, ISMN 30, ASA 81, imatinib 400 daily, capecitabine 1000 BID d1-14 q21d. NKDA.
Exam: BP above goal. Well appearing. HEENT normal. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, healed incisions, no mass. No edema. Skin without bruising. Mild postural tremor.
A/P
- HTN above goal on lisinopril/HCTZ. BMP.
- Stage IV colon adenocarcinoma, CML: oncology/hematology.
- CAD with stable angina, pAF: stable, cardiology yearly.
- Essential tremor, ED: unchanged.
- Lipids, A1c. PHQ-2 0. Flu/COVID in the fall.
RTC 3 mo.
